correctness.rationale: Stanley facet normals form a totally unimodular signed incidence matrix, making smooth cones exactly feasible forest-normal cones. The proof classifies all induced minimal feasible cycle blocks of the bounded-crown cover graph as the boundary K2,n-1, the internal disjoint-index four-cycles, or equal-index triple six-cycles; no >=8 induced cycles exist because each lower vertex misses only its paired upper neighbor. Integral primitive ray relations identify Segre (P1)^(n-1), 2x2 rank-one conifold, and 3x3 rank-one determinantal generic transverse semigroups; dimensions and multiplicities follow. All families meet in the diagonal P1 face. The explicit exhaustive face checker agrees for n=3,4, checks predicted cones/fixed vertices for n=5; n=5 enumeration is not exhaustive and finite experiments do not establish the theorem.

originality.rationale: The general Hibi forest criterion and generic cycle/Segre methods are prior work. The concrete all-parameter bounded-crown classification with three irreducible-component families, their codimensions and different generic transverse Segre determinantal models, universal P1 intersection, and exact smooth fixed-point count is neither stated in inspected primary sections nor implied by the recoverable different-object prior claims. Targeted mathematical record searches found no equivalent, but missing full Wagner text presents material residual originality risk. This is a qualified self-review, not proof of global uniqueness.

value.rationale: The bounded crown is a natural infinite family of order-polytopal Hibi toric varieties with a missing matching in its height-two middle comparability graph. The exact, heterogeneous singular locus quantifies a sharp non-pure phenomenon absent in pure Grassmann Hibi examples: n-dependent boundary Segre cones, codimension-three conifold components, codimension-five 3x3 determinantal components, a common intersection line and a unique smooth fixed point. These data answer natural local and global singular geometry questions rather than arbitrary parameter slices or simple substitutions.
